_what: Provider-price provenance for the media estimator. Historical rows remain priceable; the current video default is standard Seedance 2.0.
_how_to_refresh: Read the exact OpenRouter video-model catalogue and pricing page, preserve historical rows, then run media.test.ts. Seedance nominal token pricing and policy allowance are separate; no guaranteed provider invoice ceiling is established. Image pricing remains measured as recorded in the Phase33.1 evidence.
source: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models (each entry carries its own vendor page)

entries.unit: Nominal USD per output video-second at 720x1280, 24fps; reservation adds one second per submitted clip

vendor.pricingInfoOverride: OpenRouter standard Seedance 2.0 charges $7.00 per million video tokens, with or without audio. The published H*W*duration*24/1024 formula implies $0.1512 per second at 720x1280. Current catalogue verified 2026-10-24. Actual output tokens determine billing; no upper frame-count guarantee was found.

reservation.basis: Owner-reviewed policy allowance for actual-output frame variance, not an established provider maximum

entries.notes: Exact standard model, not Mini/Fast. Current admission prices only720p,4..15seconds. Historical Grok remains priceable. $3.50 job and12 generated-second ceilings unchanged.

entries.unit: USD per output video-second, per resolution

vendor.pricingInfoOverride: xAI's Grok Imagine video on OpenRouter costs $0.05 per second at 480p and $0.07 per second at 720p, for durations of 1 to 15 seconds (any integer). READ 2026-08-30 from openrouter.ai/x-ai/grok-imagine-video, and corroborated the same day by a live paid call: duration 5 at 480p returned usage.cost 0.25, exactly 5 x $0.05.

entries.notes: Route-qualified id: the video plane posts to openrouter.ai/api/v1/videos and the id travels unstripped. No 1080p rate is published, so a 1080p request is unknown_model rather than a silent downgrade. The 1-15 grid is the reason this counterparty was accepted - see ADR-027. Historical price row retained after the standard Seedance default migration; never a fallback.

vendor.pricingInfoOverride: tts-1 costs $15.00 per 1 million characters ($0.015 per 1000 characters).

entries.notes: The adapter pins WAV output, voice, and speed 1.
Verbose JSON with word timestamps is requested for caption timing.

vendor.pricingInfoOverride: MEASURED, not quoted: one live OpenRouter call on 2026-08-30 for a 1024x1536 quality:low image returned usage.cost $0.004875 (image_tokens 158 = $0.004740 fixed, plus $0.000135 for a 27-token prompt). Reserved at $0.006 - the extra $0.001125 is prompt-token headroom for ~225 further tokens.

entries.notes: Route-qualified id: the still plane posts to openrouter.ai/api/v1/images and the id travels unstripped. The adapter pins size 1024x1536, quality low, n 1, output_format png. size and NOT aspect_ratio - the same probe showed they are not interchangeable (aspect_ratio 9:16 returns 864x1536 at $0.003735), and the cheaper, better-composed 9:16 option is deferred to its own phase because it changes what every still looks like.

sceneKinds._what: 20.2 §2.3 / ADR-019 — the per-scene-kind economics the scene contract is justified by.
sceneKinds._derived: DERIVED from the provider entries above, not separately sourced. media.test.ts recomputes every number here from the live tables, so the ADR's arithmetic cannot rot silently while a price row moves.

perScene.note: A free-library clip. It BUYS a line (a mediaJobs row and landed bytes) at a price of zero — unlike uploaded_video/text_card, whose `buys` is null because nothing is fetched at all.
A free-library photograph, panned like an animated_image but at zero.

reel30s._what: Separate-mode standard Seedance policy reservations, preserving historical worked scene decks and legacy ceilings. Explicit native production is recorded separately below. These are policy estimates, not guaranteed provider invoices.

mixed.scenes: 3 generated x 4s + 4 stills x 4s + 1 card x 2s
mixed._generatedSeconds: 3 x 4 s = 12, which is EXACTLY MEDIA_GENERATED_SECONDS_CAP. This deck sits ON the boundary with zero slack - a one-second nudge to any generated scene makes it illegal - and media.test.ts asserts that deliberately, because the cap was chosen to keep this deck and media-director.md's worked answer legal as written.

generatedOnly.why: A 30-second all-generated deck requires30 generated seconds and is refused by the unchanged12-second cap. Two15-second standard clips would reserve$4.8384 including per-clip policy allowance, also above the unchanged$3.50job cap; the generated-seconds check runs first.

stockLeaning.scenes: 1 generated x 4s + 3 stock_video x 6s + 1 stock_image x 8s
stockLeaning._what: One4-second standard Seedance clip reserves$0.756 including policy headroom; stock assets have zero provider cost.

sceneKinds._targetsUnreachableByGeneratedVideoAlone: Legacy/separate audio uses the12-requested-generated-second cap and cannot fill any target solely with generated clips. Explicit native mode instead permits30/45/60seconds under separate60second/$15whole-job policy; tenant/deployment rails remain.

native.basis: 15four-second clips, each reserving5nominal seconds at$0.1512; render/captions additional. Policy allowances are not guaranteed provider invoices.
